long_biography.plain_text:
Holmgren entered film without formal training, first serving an unpaid trial with a Swedish corporate-film producer. After an early partnership dissolved, he borrowed against everything he owned to launch Mekano just as Sweden opened television to advertising. The company expanded rapidly into commercials, programmes and feature films before he sold it.

Relocating to Mallorca, Holmgren and his wife Grete created Palma Pictures in 1993. They built relationships with local authorities, secured equipment, assembled a permanent crew and eventually developed a large studio complex capable of handling location and stage work together. That infrastructure helped Mallorca compete for international productions and created a lasting screen-services industry on the island. The couple sold the company in 2006, and Holmgren later received Mallorca's Jaume II prize for promoting the island internationally.
